summary: A 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS profile data shows an 86.0% time-in-range with stable glycemic variability (CV 32.6%). While overnight stability is generally good, mild nocturnal hypoglycemia (5.1% below 70 mg/dL) occurs during early-morning hours, and postprandial hyperglycemia appears in the late afternoon (15:00–17:00). The closed-loop system relies heavily on UAM and SMB automation with zero explicit carbohydrate entries recorded in the treatment summary.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7% with 3,995 valid entries over 14 days and robust device telemetry.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries, 10 gaps (largest 65 min), 2,315 treatments, 6,214 device statuses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero explicit carb treatment entries in telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: Time in range is 86.0%, time above range is 8.9%, time below range is 5.1%, with CV at 32.6%.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose summary average 121.6 mg/dL, standard deviation 39.7 mg/dL, extremes from 41 to 293 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight glucose dips during local hours 00:00–02:00 while late afternoon hours 15:00–17:00 show average glucose rising above 148–162 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose averages, daily glucose rows, and basal profile segments (0.5 to 0.8 U/h).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unannounced or unlogged meals during afternoon hours.

analysis_steps.findings: Static ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U across a single segment, carb ratios range from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U, and DIA is 10 hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS profile parameters for ISF, CR segments, and DIA.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and operating correctly under Oref1 with 3-minute delivery intervals.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS profile smb_settings and loop status telemetry showing frequent microbolus activity.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is active at 70% adjustment, compensating for a flat static ISF.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS profile sensitivity settings and loop sensitivity ratio telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: No manual meal boluses or prebolus declarations are recorded in telemetry, indicating complete reliance on UAM and SMB.
analysis_steps.evidence: Treatment summary carb entries = 0 g and declared analysis_context meal strategies empty.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No recorded meal carb entries or bolus timing logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb absorption is governed by a 7-hour max window and 8 mg/dL/5 min impact threshold, handling unannounced glucose excursions reactively.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS carb absorption settings and UAM loop responses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal composition and structured extended carb data.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight hypoglycemia and afternoon hyperglycemia can be addressed by sequential profile verification and optional meal logging before adjusting insulin parameters.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined telemetry trends, loop status logs, and profile settings.

strengths: High CGM data quality and coverage (98.7%).
Strong overall time-in-range of 86.0% with stable glycemic variability (CV 32.6%).
Effective Oref1 closed-loop automation with UAM and SMB handling unannounced glucose excursions.
issues: Hypoglycemia time below range (5.1% <70 mg/dL) exceeds standard clinical safety targets, concentrated overnight.
Postprandial hyperglycemia peaks in the late afternoon (local hours 15:00–17:00).
Complete absence of logged carbohydrate entries limits closed-loop prediction accuracy.

recommendations.title: Verify Overnight Basal Rates
recommendations.description: Observe overnight glucose trends between 00:00 and 03:00 to determine if current basal rates (0.6 to 0.8 U/h) contribute to nocturnal dips.

recommendations.title: Introduce Manual Carbohydrate Logging
recommendations.description: Logging meals manually will improve Oref1 prediction accuracy and reduce reliance on reactive UAM corrections.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings maintain an 86% TIR, and closed-loop automation actively manages glucose excursions. Changes should be withheld until manual meal logging provides clearer postprandial data.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight hypoglycemia and afternoon glucose peaks while logging carbohydrate intake for at least 3 to 5 meals.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings and verify basal and meal responses over the next week before making adjustments.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight readings show mild dips, but closed-loop automation is actively managing delivery; verify stability before changing.
Current morning basal rate supports stable early-morning baseline trends.
Rate supports morning transition without excessive stacking.
Midday basal segment maintains stable glucose prior to afternoon rises.
Afternoon rise correlates with unlogged meals rather than definitive basal deficit.
Rate provides appropriate transition into evening hours.
Maintains stable evening baseline before night routines.
No carb data available to evaluate ratio performance; keep current setting.
Maintains stable early morning ratio without direct evidence of postprandial failure.
Daytime carb ratio operates alongside UAM; verify with manual logging first.
Afternoon ratio should be evaluated after recording actual carbohydrate intake.
Evening carb ratio maintains stable night-time entry.
Dynamic ISF is currently scaling insulin sensitivity dynamically; flat ISF should not be altered without baseline testing.
90 mg/dL target aligns with tight closed-loop control.
100 mg/dL daytime target provides appropriate buffer against hypoglycemia.
90 mg/dL evening target supports stable overnight transition.
10-hour duration of insulin activity matches slow Oref1 insulin action modeling.
Both SMB and UAM are appropriately enabled for closed-loop automation.
Activation settings support aggressive automated correction without requiring manual carb entry.
3-minute interval and max basal minute caps provide responsive microbolusing.
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Safety limits provide adequate headroom while capping maximum insulin delivery.
Dynamic ISF at 70% effectively scales sensitivity without requiring autosens target changes.
Absorption settings support UAM detection effectively.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Telemetry indicates complete reliance on closed-loop UAM and SMB automation with zero logged carbohydrate entries, leading to reactive postprandial management.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Continue utilizing Oref1 automation while beginning to log carbohydrate grams manually for meals to improve prediction accuracy and blunt afternoon postprandial peaks.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record carbohydrate intake for at least 3 to 5 meals over the coming week to evaluate how Oref1 responds to actual meal-bolus dynamics.

implementation_steps: Verify overnight basal rates and observe whether nocturnal hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) persists.
Begin logging carbohydrate intake manually for a subset of meals to evaluate postprandial automation responses.
Monitor afternoon glucose trends (15:00–17:00) after introducing meal logging before considering any profile adjustments.
education: Unannounced meal (UAM) and super microbolus (SMB) features allow closed-loop systems to react to glucose rises without manual carb entries, but logging carbs improves prediction accuracy.
Dynamic ISF scales insulin sensitivity based on recent glucose deltas, helping compensate for a flat static ISF profile.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
